Ramps are generated in OKLCH around the three colours already in the Tapio

palettes.$comment: Colour in a chart does one of four jobs; each job has one palette. Red is excluded from the categorical slots — it is the alarm channel and nothing else.

scatter_safe.$comment: Any two marks can end up adjacent in a scatter, so every pair must separate — not just neighbours. Under that test the palette caps at three: violet, teal, amber. Brand blue is held out because it collapses against teal under deuteranopia.

recency.$comment: Stacked profiles: the newest at full weight, the older stepping down the blue ramp, oldest lightest. Recency is an order and the reader should see the order in the colour, so this is an ordinal ramp and not eight categorical hues. Every step stays clear of the accent so the mean profile is never mistaken for one of its own members.

sequential.$comment: One hue, light to dark, for spectrograms, heatmaps and stacked-recency profiles. Reversed in dark so low magnitude sits nearest the surface.

diverging.$comment: Blue to gold with a neutral midpoint, because red is reserved. Blue is the positive pole.

status.$comment: Fixed meanings, never themed into a series slot, always shipped with an icon and a label.

radius.$comment: 4 is the default (buttons, inputs, tabs); 8 for cards, panels and dialogs; 0 for anything that tiles. Plot areas are square-cornered — a rounded plot frame reads as a card and the corner clips real data.

motion.$comment: Measured values never animate. Progress through a measurement animates; the result does not.

metrics.$comment: One layout. The system's density scale exists so one token set can serve a lab desktop, a mill-floor tablet and a handheld; RollView is the first of those and only the first, so it carries that row rather than a table to choose from. A touch or handheld build would raise these — row 56/control 48/target 48/text 17 for the mill floor, 64/64/64/19 for a gloved hand.

elevation.$comment: Depth is carried by borders and surface lightness first, shadow second. In dark, elevation is a lighter surface plus a border — a black shadow on a near-black ground is invisible.
